Transactions of the American Fisheries Society 97(1): 28–31. Report: 'Some observations of food selectivity by northern pike and bowfins in aquaria', Michigan Department of Conservation Research and Development Report No. 28 = Institute for Fisheries Research Report No. 1704, May 21, 1965, Dingell-Johnson Project F-27-R; 17 PDF pages. The entry's 'First issued 1965 as Michigan Institute for Fisheries Research Report 1704 (= R&D Report 28)' is right. The report covers bowfins too; the article's title names only pike, so it may be shortened.

claims.claim: in aquaria, a pike that readily ate green sunfish would not attack bullheads; the only pike that ate a bullhead did so after other food ran out, and it died when a pectoral spine punctured its stomach (Beyerle & Williams 1968)
claims.note: Article not read. The stand-in report supports every part (report p. 7, PDF p. 7): 'A pike often showed interest in a swimming bullhead but would not attack it. Only one bullhead was eaten by a pike, after the other available food had been consumed, and this pike died soon after a pectoral spine punctured its stomach.' Table 1 (report p. 14, read on the page image): one 11.5-inch pike offered 10 green sunfish (mean 2.1 in) and 10 bullheads (2.2 in) ate all 10 sunfish and no bullhead (P < 0.001). Conditions: tanks and aquaria with no cover; equal numbers (usually five or fewer at a time) of two or three prey kinds introduced together, eaten prey not replaced; bullheads were Ictalurus spp.; the authors caution that the results measure selectivity driven by prey behaviour (accessibility) more than innate preference (report pp. 5–7).

notes: Recommend citing the stand-in, which is free and is the authors' own full account: Beyerle, G. B. & Williams, J. E. 1965. Some observations of food selectivity by northern pike and bowfins in aquaria. Michigan Department of Conservation, Institute for Fisheries Research Report No. 1704 (Research and Development Report No. 28). Its other findings (abstract, report p. 1): pike chose minnows and chubsuckers over centrarchids and yellow perch, showed no choice between centrarchids and yellow perch, and chose centrarchids over bullheads; bowfins took bottom-dwelling prey (crayfish, chubsuckers) and caught mid-water golden shiners least; the authors conclude that large stocks of soft-rayed forage fishes favour pike growth and doubt pike or bowfins can control panfish. The pike in the Table 1 rows on report p. 14 were 6.2–27.9 inches long.
